subject: FinBridge GDPR checklist and role-split confirmation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Muller <anna.muller@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap: GDPR scope, DPA ask, and SCC options

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single thread to track: 

1) GDPR scope & roles
- During the call you indicated FinBridge will act as the controller for customer data processed through your payment flows. We want to confirm whether you'll accept Redwood as a processor for transactional metadata and model inference output, or whether you need Redwood to be a joint-controller for any enrichment use-cases.

2) SCC module
- We're seeing two paths that fit the procurement team’s preference: Module 2 (processor scenario) or Module 3 (joint-controller scenario). Each has slightly different obligations and evidence requirements.

3) Evidence requests
- To progress I’ll attach our brief security questionnaire and a draft DPA. Could you (or procurement) confirm the SOC 2 scope you need (Type II latest report, encryption-at-rest key management details, data retention windows)?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Anna / procurement: confirm controller/processor decision and SOC 2 expectations by EOD Wednesday (2026-09-22).
- FinBridge: return the completed questionnaire (attached) and indicate preferred SCC module.
- Redwood legal (cc Marissa): will produce a DPA draft aligned with the selected SCC module after we get confirmation.

Attachments: FinBridge_Security_Questionnaire_2026.pdf (fillable), RBW-DPA-draft-v1.docx (placeholder draft)

If you prefer, we can run a short procurement-only call to walk through the SCC options.

Best,
Ben
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0118

From: Anna Muller <anna.muller@finbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finbridge.com
Date: 2026-09-17T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: GDPR scope, DPA ask, and SCC options

Thanks Ben — appreciate the summary. Quick clarifications from procurement: 

- FinBridge will be controller for the end-customer transaction data (obvious). We are open to designating Redwood as a processor for the inference service that returns labeling/classification outputs we feed into our workflows, provided the DPA limits processing to those outputs and the raw input (no retention beyond 30 days).
- If Redwood needs to use data for model improvement, that must be opt-in and scoped.
- For procurement, preferred SCC module is Module 2 (processor scenario). We can escalate to Module 3 only if legal requires joint responsibilities after reviewing the DPA draft.

SOC 2: procurement requires latest Type II report and a summary of the scope (which services were in-scope). Also confirm encryption at rest: are keys customer-managed (KMS) or managed by Redwood?

We'll try to return the filled questionnaire by end of day Thursday.

Anna Muller
Head of Procurement, FinBridge
anna.muller@finbridge.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Muller <anna.muller@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T08:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: GDPR scope, DPA ask, and SCC options

Great — thanks for the confirmation and the Module 2 preference. A couple follow-ups from our side: 

- Retention & model improvement: Redwood can accept processor-only role for the production inference path. We'll add a hard 30-day retention clause and an explicit clause that we will not train or improve models on FinBridge data without separate written opt-in.
- KMS: Redwood offers both options. For FinBridge we can either integrate with your cloud KMS (customer-managed) or use our managed KMS. For procurement would you prefer the customer-managed KMS option? If yes, please share desired cloud provider (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- SOC 2: I'll route the request to Diego and Marissa. Diego will reply with the summary and Marissa will attach the redlineable DPA after we hear back from you.

Next steps:
- FinBridge: completed questionnaire + KMS preference (target: 2026-09-21)
- Redwood: Diego to supply SOC 2 scope summary; Marissa to prepare DPA draft tailored to Module 2 (target: 2026-09-22)

Sending the updated questionnaire again in case procurement needs the editable version.

Cheers,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Muller <anna.muller@finbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T15:48:00Z
Subject: DPA draft approach and evidence list (Module 2)

Hi Anna — following Ben’s note and your preference for Module 2, legal has prepared guidance for what we would include in the DPA and what evidence procurement should expect. Summary below; I’ll attach the redlineable DPA within 24 hours once we hear back on KMS preference and receive the completed questionnaire.

Redwood proposed DPA highlights (processor / Module 2):
- Purpose limitation: processing limited to inference and ephemeral metadata to support the service.
- Retention: default 30 days for raw inputs and inference outputs; logs for billing kept up to 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- No-model-training clause: explicit prohibition on using FinBridge data for model improvement unless and until FinBridge opts in via separate contract.
- Subprocessor list: standard list plus notification/resubmission process for critical subprocessors.
- Technical & organizational measures: reference SOC 2 controls, encryption in transit and at rest, access controls and audit logging requirements.

Evidence requested by procurement (minimum):
- Latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted permissible) and SOC 2 scope statement.
- Encryption-in-rest architecture doc or short blurb specifying KMS model (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
- Public or shared pen-test summary and remediation tracker (redacted OK).
- Data flow diagram showing where PII crosses boundaries and whether any inference outputs are stored outside EU regions.

If you confirm Module 2 and agree to the retention and no-training language, we will:
1) Attach the DPA draft for review (RBW-DPA-draft-v1.docx).
2) Provide SOC 2 scope summary and a link to the report under controlled access.
3) Share a short data flow diagram for your security review.

Action items (to close the procurement gate):
- FinBridge: return questionnaire + KMS preference + confirm acceptance of retention/no-training by 2026-09-24.
- Redwood: Marissa to send DPA draft within 24 hours of FinBridge confirmation; Diego to share SOC 2 scope doc.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk legal and procurement through any paragraph in the DPA.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: RBW-DPA-draft-v1.docx (to follow), FinBridge_Security_Questionnaire_2026.pdf (resend)
